# infrawrench_cost_annotation (Resource)

A note pinned to a date or a span on cost charts — the migration, the instance-type change, the customer that onboarded — so the step in the graph has an explanation next to it rather than in somebody's memory.

Managing these in Terraform is worth it when the event is already a Terraform change: the same pull request that resizes the fleet can annotate the day it happened.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `start_date` (String) Inclusive first day (UTC) the note is about, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. It is mapped to whichever bucket holds it at the chart's binning — daily and cumulative use the day itself, weekly the Monday that starts its week, monthly the first of its month.
- `text` (String) The note, 1–500 characters.

### Optional

- `cost_report_id` (String) The report this note is scoped to. Omit it for an **org-wide** note, which is the useful default: an org-wide note is drawn on every cost chart, because "we changed instance types" is not a fact about one report.
- `end_date` (String) Inclusive last day, or omitted for a note about a single moment. A deploy is a moment; a migration is a week, and a week spelled as seven notes misstates how many things happened.

An end equal to the start is stored as null, so writing the same day twice reads back as a moment. Set `end_date` only when it genuinely differs from `start_date`.

### Read-Only

- `cost_anomaly_id` (String) The detected cost anomaly this note explains, or null for a note written by hand — which is every note Terraform creates.

Read-only, and there is no way to set it: the link is minted server-side when somebody acknowledges an anomaly with an explanation, and that acknowledgement writes its own annotation. Adopting one of those into Terraform is possible but rarely what you want; the explanation belongs to whoever investigated the spike.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned annotation id. Use it with `terraform import`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is in the URL when you open the object in the app, and in the
# --json output of the Infrawrench CLI.
terraform import infrawrench_cost_annotation.example 0c1d2e3f-4a5b-6c7d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
```
